issue_context.title: Async style with reply.send
issue_context.body:
## 🐛 Bug Report

`repl.send` inside an async function has created a lot of headache.

- https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/238
- https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/238
- https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/548
- https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/1131

with https://github.com/fastify/fastify-static/issues/110 we have another issue. The issue ist that an error is logged because `sendFile` doesn't accept a callback or return a promise. The route is fulfilled to `undefined` before the file was sent. This behaviour doesn't agree with https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/master/docs/Routes.md#promise-resolution.

Due to the current implementation every decorator/plugin which calls `.send` under the hood must provide a callback or promise to the consumer. If they don't the handler can't use async/await and will loose the control over the response.

## Expected behavior

**In the longer term we change the api.**
```js
// the data flow isnt determined by the function return value (koajs be like)
fastify
  .get('/', async (request, reply) => {
    reply.body = await data()
	repl.body = sync()
  });
```
**In short term:**
Teach and update the docs that you can use only `reply.send` in async/await if you still return a promise that controls the asynchronous operation.
```js
until send is called
fastify
  .get('/', async (request, reply) => {
    return op().then(reply.send)
  });
```
or we recommend to not use `rely.send` at all in async functions
comments: The async operations have nothing to do with _sending_ the response, only building the response. I’m not listing a complete example here because it is beside the point. Which is: `reply.send` should work regardless of the function declaration.

The best example how it should work is Hapi.js :smiley_cat: They always returned a `Response` object which is build by the request `tooklit` OR a javascript value. They removed callback-style from the landscape because you can always promisify it.

That's no real use case it's your favorite way to write code. 

You can just return the value and in case of error you can return the value with an rejected promise OR throw an error.

> Simply returning the resolution, or rejection, of a promise is not sufficient in all cases.

Hapi removed callback style in route handlers and Hapi is driven by a big community and enterprise users and this is significant.
Amazing. I can't even begin to respond in a cordial manner to this.
I don't want to be rude. I just want to convince you. You talked about use cases which can be handled only with reply.send which ones?

@mcollina what's the motivation of using `reply.send()` in an async function? Just to allow mixing different styles? I don't get it :confused:

Only to ensure: I'm talking about the future fastify v3-4 not to patch the current codebase. For the current state I created a [PR](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/1868) to improve the documentation around Promise/async-await usage.

> @mcollina what's the motivation of using reply.send() in an async function? Just to allow mixing different styles? I don't get it 😕

When interacting with other library it's almost impossible to avoid. The proposed syntax will not work with the `sendFile` issue for example, as we will have to wait anyway for `send` to finish. By making `reply` awaitable, we can provide an escape hatch for all those cases without making any significant change to our APIs.

I agree with @mcollina, there are some cases where you need to use `reply.send`, and Fastify is designed to allow you to use both callbacks and promises style.
Another case that we will fix with this change, is to enable an easier support for async style handlers with [`point-of-view`](https://github.com/fastify/point-of-view).
Making `reply` a thenable might bot be the perfect solution, but it solves in a smart way the problem.
@mcollina OK you are talking about scenarios to avoid promisify things right? I'm fine with that proposal even when it makes the api more complicated.

> @mcollina OK you are talking about scenarios to avoid promisify things right? I'm fine with that proposal even when it makes the api more complicated.

Yes. This is both the case of `point-of-view` and `fastify-static`. Promisifying is often an all-or-nothing choice, and there are plenty of cases where it's impractical.
Thank you @mcollina for stepping in here. I appreciate a level head recognizing the problem and offering up an excellent solution.
Thanks!

Actually... to implement something like this, I would not immediatly send the email from the handler. 

I would actually create a "Queue", where you put the otpEmails into the queue. The processor the queue tries to send the email, and if it fails retries. By decoupling this, you can solve this imho better.
